title: Portable Reality
subtitle: Truth is correctness ... Hey, is anyone going to guarantee the truth of this statement?

items.text: Forest, Toybox
A "professional" expedition team of one investigator and two researchers trudges through the woods.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: We've encountered more and more Critters since we entered this forest.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: At least we didn't come here for nothing.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hey, Ulrich. Don't forget our loot.
His fellow researcher stares at him incredulously.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: "Loot"? Adler, are you seriously calling these supplies "loot"?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I didn't expect you of all people to start indulging in roleplay.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I don't know what you're talking about.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And you can save your energy for the journey. We still have a long way ahead of us.
Sensing another argument brewing, Marcus cuts in.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Mr. Enigma, Mr. Ulrich, perhaps we should hurry.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So we can get there before the "language disorder" spreads to all of Laplace.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ah, good. At least someone in our party can put together a rational thought.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: According to Musae's map, we still have seven kilometers until we reach the toybox's depths.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If we cross this Critter's territory, we'll save a third of the time it would take to go around—
Suddenly, a strange noise interrupts her.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Is that a Critter?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No, it's an arcanist using Critter-Speech.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Looks like another piece afflicted with the "language disorder."
Marcus stares at the arcanist and frowns.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: We're too far away. I can't make out what he's trying to say.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Let's get closer. I may be able to "read" some useful information.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Alright. Allow me.
The trek ends with a tall building peeking out from beyond the trees.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Goodness, this really was a shortcut!
Enigma glances at her. Marcus is excitedly checking what's ahead, a far cry from that head-down figure he vaguely remembers.
Yes, the spitting image of a brave investigator. A mountaineer. A ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm very grateful for your help, Ms. Marcus. I wager we'd still be running in circles if you weren't here.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Indeed. If we can maintain this rate of progress ...

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We'll be submitting an up-to-standard Pre-Storm Protocol very, very soon.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ulrich, why didn't you submit this copy of the Pre-Storm Protocol?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Half-finished products have no place in a conference, Adler.
Faced with the substitute director's aggressive interrogation, Ulrich only watches as the file is slammed onto the desk.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: It simply isn't persuasive enough. The toybox's "Storm" simulation still poses some problems that require solving.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Am I hearing this right, blob-for-brains? You're telling me you've already finished the damn thing, but you thought you'd play us all for laughs for a while?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Urgh, just turn it in, damn it! Shut those checkered chumps up!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: As I said, there are still some problems that haven't—

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ulrich, you're slipping into the mindset of a "creator."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: They're simulated data. There's no need for your "humanitarian care."

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: And YOUR biases are showing, Adler.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: As you'll recall from your encounters with the many familiar faces in the toybox, the pieces there are not objectively different from their real-world counterparts.
Familiar faces.
No. None of this is real.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: They're just pieces of data. Parts of a simulation.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You shut yourself in your labs, in the toybox, calculating all day. And for what?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If you all keep playing "delusional genius" and continue to ignore the problems Laplace is facing, soon it will be out of our hands.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This isn't the toybox. There are no resets.
A brief silence falls over the meeting room. Then, the researchers catch on to a certain keyword.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It's true, Adler. With every new era brought by the "Storm," the Foundation has only tightened their policies. Perhaps to an extreme.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: However, they need Laplace's research results. They need our innovation, our inventions.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: The Foundation doesn't view us as an enemy.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Exactly. I seriously don't get you guys. It's not like it'll affect us, so quit wasting our time with all these meetings!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: So what if Laplace loses its independence?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Adler, we can't properly discuss the issue if you don't explain what's making you so apprehensive.
Enigma's mouth opens. A habitual scoff slips out before any words can.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hah. If the Foundation passes their "Storm" personnel reform, do you really think you'll be able to continue your research freely?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Laplace is this close to being completely subsumed by the Foundation! When that happens, where do you think our inventions are going to be used?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Don't tell me that none of you have ever considered—

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh la la, no wonder they called you Enigma! If you've got some insider information, just tell us already!
The substitute director draws a deep breath.
Office, Foundation

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Adler Hofmann, you've arrived. Please, sit.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No need. I'm not here to chat.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Fine by me. Then allow me to move on to the subject: how's your progress on the "Storm" contingency plan the Foundation requested?
Enigma waves the question away impatiently.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Get to the point.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: I had planned on some small talk, but I'll get right to it if you wish.
She leans back in her chair.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: If you assume the position of Laplace's next director, I can promise that the Foundation will not significantly interfere with the LSCC's regular operations.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: On the condition I obey your every word?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Quite the opposite. Everything will be in your hands, to do with as you see fit.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then I would choose to keep things the way they are.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And there are plenty of more outstanding—more rational—members who could take on the responsibility.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Take Ulrich, the leader of the "Storm" Research Group, for example. Or Pointer—she did remarkable work on developing the teleport disk. Among any number of others.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Mr. Adler, I'm afraid you've missed a crucial point.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Although Committee Member Irinei is the one pushing for the "Storm" personnel reform, appointing you as the director of Laplace is not his intention.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's yours, isn't it, Madam Constantine?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: You see, a keen mind is a key prerequisite to becoming director.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The core of the issue isn't how the Foundation presents its final decision to the outside world, but who we present. And what we need is a "human." A stable, persuasive, uncontroversial human.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: When all is said and done, the Foundation's objective remains the same. We only wish to do all we can to brave the "Storm."

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: In this regard, you are the best choice, Mr. Adler.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Your best choice was forced to retire in the Timekeeper's Suitcase.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Ah, yes. Madam Lucy has certainly been enjoying a comfortable vacation.
Maintaining her smile, Constantine steers the conversation in another direction.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: But let's not dwell on that. There's something else I wanted to tell you. Something interesting—to be kept to yourself for the time being, of course. It's a research topic we haven't yet revealed to Laplace.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: As you're well aware, for many years we've been searching for a method to bring back those reversed in the "Storm."

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Well, the Foundation has discovered a feasible theory: if we can inject a person's past memories into a suitable body, then we can restore those who were lost.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: All those years ago, a special candidate helped us in the first stages of this experiment. And now, we're finally starting to see results.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: To this end, we hope to acquire help from Laplace.
